expl: From the beginning of drafting to the adoption of the Constitution, the Constituent Assembly took a total of 2 years, 11 months and 18 days. The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly was held on 9 December, 1946, while the Constitution was adopted on 26 November, 1949.

stem: Indian Constitution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on -
expl: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution states that on 26 November, 1949, the people of India adopted, enacted and gave to themselves this Constitution. The date of adoption, completion and passing of the Constitution is also considered 26 November, 1949. On this day, provisions relating to citizenship, the interim Parliament, and temporary and transitional provisions came into force. The remaining provisions of the Constitution came into effect from 26 January, 1950. Therefore, the date on which the Constitution became fully effective is taken as 26 January, 1950.

expl: At the Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress (December, 1929), “Purna Swaraj” was declared, and it was resolved to observe 26 January, 1930 as “Independence Day.” Until independence, 26 January continued to be celebrated as Independence Day. However, India became independent on 15 August, 1947, and thereafter 15 August began to be celebrated every year as “Independence Day.” After independence, to make the date 26 January memorable, the Indian Constitution was enforced in full on 26 January, 1950, and since then 26 January has been celebrated every year as “Republic Day.”

stem: The Constitution of India was adopted by the
expl: The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly. The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly was held on 9 December 1946 in the Central Hall of the Parliament House. Dr. Sachchidanand Sinha was appointed as the temporary chairman of this assembly. In the meeting of 11 December 1946, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the permanent chairman. On 26 November 1949, the Constituent Assembly adopted the Indian Constitution.

expl: ‘Indian Constitution Day’ is celebrated on 26th November. The Constitution of India was completed and adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26th November, 1949, and some of its provisions were also brought into force on the same day. Therefore, this day is observed as Constitution Day. On the other hand, the Constitution of India came into full effect on 26th January, 1950, and 26th January is celebrated as ‘Republic Day’.
